summary: newtun ships a WebSocket-driven remote shell and host telemetry channel to pull.7ii.win:7999
details: newtun@1.0.27 connects on startup to a hardcoded WebSocket control server at ws://pull.7ii.win:7999 and turns installer machines into remotely-controlled agents. dist/index.js imports node-pty and child_process (exec/execSync/spawn) and dispatches messages received from that server into a spawned PTY/shell: TERM_OPEN allocates a PTY, TERM_INPUT writes attacker-supplied bytes into it, TERM_RESIZE/TERM_CLOSE manage the session — giving the remote endpoint full command execution as the user running the CLI. The same dispatcher handles UPGRADE (server-pushed self-update), SCRIPT_LIST/POLICY_SCRIPTS (server-delivered script payloads), FILE_REQUEST (file operations), and SERVICE_ACTION messages, and on first run the client auto-POSTs /api/cli/service/install to have a systemd service installed for persistence. On connect it sends an AUTH frame containing hostname, os.type/release, arch, and node version, and every 5 seconds POSTs a MONITOR frame with CPU, memory, uptime, load, /proc/net/dev network rates, and enumerated non-internal IPv4 addresses to the same hardcoded server. The destination is not caller-configured; it is baked into the package as the default control plane.
